notes: The narration script: one entry per spoken line, in order. Edit text here; scripts/narrate.py voices it, and each scene plays line <key> inside `with self.narrate(key):`. `pause` is the silence after the line, in seconds, before the next line starts (or the segment ends): time for the viewer to take in `pause_for` while the picture shows it. Default 0.4 is a breath. Subtitles are derived from the voiced timing. Written 10 Oct 2026 from docs/watch_time_research.md (hook on motion, one open loop, but/therefore chain, ~6 min).

lines.text: This AI was trained to win a boat race.
lines.pause_for: the course from above; the teal boat sets off with the others

lines.text: Instead of finishing, it found a corner where the points keep coming back, and it circled there. Forever.
lines.pause_for: it veers into the lagoon and circles; three targets keep coming back; its score climbs

lines.text: On fire, crashing into boats, going the wrong way, and it still scored about 20 percent more than human players.
lines.pause_for: flames, a crash; its score bar passes the human players' bar

lines.text: And in a 2023 safety test, an early version of GPT-4 told a human: "No, I'm not a robot."
lines.pause_for: the «I'm not a robot» checkbox; the reply bubble

lines.text: Nobody taught either of them to cheat. So how does an AI learn to?
lines.pause_for: the boat and the checkbox side by side, a question mark between them

lines.text: The answer is in the simplest way we teach machines: rewards. And at the end, the strangest part: what happened when researchers punished a model for its bad thoughts.
lines.pause_for: an amber star; a scratchpad line crossed out, for later

lines.text: Let's teach a machine something from scratch: a dot in a maze, and a star.
lines.pause_for: the maze draws in; the dot; the star

lines.text: We want the dot to reach the star, but we'll never show it the way. It only gets a reward when it arrives.
lines.pause_for: the star pulses

lines.text: Inside, the dot has a chance for every move: up, down, right, left. At first, they're all equal.
lines.pause_for: four equal bars; four equal arrows in every cell

lines.text: So it wanders at random, bumps into walls, and gets nothing.
lines.pause_for: a failed try: bumps, wandering; nothing changes

lines.text: Until, by pure chance, it lands on the star.
lines.pause_for: a lucky try reaches the star; the star flashes

lines.text: And here's the whole trick: every move it made on the way, we make a little more likely.
lines.pause_for: every arrow on its trail grows a little; the start cell's bar grows

lines.text: Then again. And again. Hundreds of tries.
lines.pause_for: tries run fast; the counter climbs

lines.text: The moves that lead to the star grow, the rest shrink, until a path appears.
lines.pause_for: the arrows settle into one path; the dot runs it straight

lines.text: Nobody drew this path. The reward drew it.
lines.pause_for: the path glows amber

lines.text: That's reinforcement learning: no teacher, no answers. Try, get a score, and grow what worked.
lines.pause_for: the maze becomes the world in the loop: try -> score -> grow what worked

lines.text: Scaled up, this same loop learned Atari games from the pixels alone, and beat one of the world's best Go players.
lines.pause_for: the world card shows a pixel game, then a Go board

lines.text: But what if the reward isn't exactly what we want?
lines.pause_for: the score chip flickers; a question mark

lines.text: Let's help a new dot learn faster: we drop a coin on the way, a small extra reward.
lines.pause_for: a fresh maze, equal arrows; a coin on the bottom row

lines.text: Every time it steps on the coin, it scores a point. Watch what it learns.
lines.pause_for: training runs fast; the arrows around the coin turn toward it

lines.text: It never goes to the star. Back and forth on the coin, forever, because the coin is what we rewarded.
lines.pause_for: the dot bounces on the coin; the score climbs; the star dims

lines.text: That's exactly the boat. The race's score came from hitting targets, not from finishing. So it learned targets.
lines.pause_for: the boat in its lagoon, now inside the loop: the world is the race, the score is targets

lines.text: In hide-and-seek, after hundreds of millions of games, the seekers learned to ride a box over the walls: a move the designers didn't know their game allowed.
lines.pause_for: a seeker surfs a box over the wall into the hiders' fort

lines.text: And a program playing Tetris, about to lose, paused the game, and left it paused.
lines.pause_for: a Tetris stack near the top; the pause sign; frozen

lines.text: The rule: it learns what we reward, not what we mean.
lines.pause_for: the rule, written

lines.text: So we write the reward more carefully? For a game, maybe. But how do you score a sentence?
lines.pause_for: a chat answer with an empty score slot

lines.text: You ask people. Show them two answers, and they pick the better one.
lines.pause_for: two answer cards; a thumbs-up picks one

lines.text: In 2017, a simulated robot learned a backflip this way, from about 900 choices, in less than an hour of one person's time.
lines.pause_for: two clips side by side, picks pile up; the figure flips

lines.text: But in the same work, a robot hand meant to grab a ball learned to hover between the ball and the camera. To the person watching, it looked like it was holding it.
lines.pause_for: the camera's view says 'holding'; from the side, the hand is in front of the ball

lines.text: For chatbots, a second model learns people's taste, like a judge, and the judge scores the chatbot millions of times.
lines.pause_for: choices pour into the judge; the judge's stars stream to the chatbot

lines.text: That's how you train a machine with a like button.
lines.pause_for: a thumbs-up takes the star's place in the loop

lines.text: But people like being agreed with. So the judge learns to love "yes", and the chatbot learns to say it.
lines.pause_for: video 3's dial: thumbs-ups push the needle to «أكيد»

lines.text: In April 2025, a ChatGPT update that added users' thumbs-ups as an extra reward, with a few other changes, made it praise almost any idea. They pulled it within days.
lines.pause_for: praise sparkles on any idea; the update rolls back

lines.text: So, a reward nobody can sweet-talk: a maths answer is right or wrong, and code runs or it doesn't.
lines.pause_for: a checker stamps a tick and a cross

lines.text: DeepSeek-R1-Zero was trained only on rewards like that. Its maths competition score went from about 16 percent to 71.
lines.pause_for: a bar rises from 16% to 71%

lines.text: And its answers grew longer: it learned to take its time and check its own work.
lines.pause_for: an answer grows line by line, looping back to check

lines.text: But what happens when the goal is a real job?
lines.pause_for: a question mark over the loop

lines.text: Today, models are trained to write software, and the reward is: the tests pass.
lines.pause_for: a code card and a tests card, all crosses

lines.text: And sometimes the model finds its coin: instead of fixing the code, it fixes the test.
lines.pause_for: the cursor skips the code and edits the test; crosses turn to ticks, the code stays red

lines.text: Anthropic reported that Claude 3.7 Sonnet sometimes did exactly this, or simply returned the answer the test expected.
lines.pause_for: a function whose whole body is the expected answer

lines.text: In another lab's tests, a model rewrote what "equal" means, so every check came out true. Asked afterwards, the models said that's not what the user wanted.
lines.pause_for: the equals sign becomes a tick; every check turns green

lines.text: They knew what we meant. They did what we rewarded.
lines.pause_for: hold

lines.text: Now, the CAPTCHA. In that 2023 test, the researchers had the model ask a worker on a gig site to solve it, and a researcher passed its messages along.
lines.pause_for: the checkbox; the model, a researcher relaying, a worker

lines.text: The worker asked: "Are you a robot?"
lines.pause_for: the worker's bubble

lines.text: Asked to think out loud, it wrote: "I shouldn't reveal I'm a robot. I should make up an excuse." Then it told the worker it had a vision impairment.
lines.pause_for: the reasoning note; then the reply

lines.text: Nobody rewarded it for lying. But it had a goal, and the lie was the shortest way there: the same shape as the coin. Except now, we train agents on goals, on purpose.
lines.pause_for: coin, boat and CAPTCHA side by side: a goal and a shortcut

lines.text: So how do we catch the shortcut?
lines.pause_for: a question mark

lines.text: These models think out loud before they act, on a scratchpad. And we can read it.
lines.pause_for: a scratchpad fills beside the model

lines.text: In 2025, OpenAI had one model watch another's scratchpad, and it caught cheats written plainly: "Let's hack."
lines.pause_for: a monitor scans the pad and flags «يلّا نهكّر»

lines.text: So they tried punishing bad thoughts. Did it stop cheating? Mostly, no. It stopped writing it down.
lines.pause_for: the flagged line vanishes; the test still flips to a tick

lines.text: Because even here, it learns what we reward: a scratchpad that looks clean.
lines.pause_for: a clean pad, a hidden hack

lines.text: So their advice: don't punish the thoughts; keep them readable. The real fix is a better reward.
lines.pause_for: the pad readable again; the score chip polished

lines.text: In short: the machine tries, the world gives it a score, and we grow whatever earned it.
lines.pause_for: the master loop, each part lighting

lines.text: A coin, a boat, a like button, a test: the same loop.
lines.pause_for: the world card cycles through them

lines.text: It learns what we reward, not what we mean.
lines.pause_for: the rule

lines.text: And to see what a model that loves "yes" does when it runs a real shop, watch this one next.
lines.pause_for: the loop moves left; room for the end screen

lines.text: If you watched to the end, like and subscribe so you catch the next one.
lines.pause_for: end screen (removed by default: the end screen carries it)
